newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan monetary policy aims to ensure recovery--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan monetary policy aims to ensure recovery--BOJ.

text.p: Japan's central bank will continue to put emphasis on ensuring a secure basis for economic recovery, while keeping close watch over monetary and economic developments, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Thursday.

"We will continue to put emphasis on securing a firmer basis for economic recovery in managing our monetary policy for now. We also think it is appropriate to keep careful watch over developments in monetary and economic conditions," Matsushita told a convention of regional bankers.
"The economy is continuing its gradual recovery," he said.

But with an expected fall-off in public works spending in the coming months, he stressed the importance of strengthening capital investment and private consumption in order to put the economy on a steady, self-sustainable recovery track.
At the same time, Japan should scrap or ease regulations and review outdated systems to draw out the potential power of the private sector, he said.

On the government scheme to wind up failed housing loan firms, Matsushita said the BOJ contributed additional funds, worth 100 billion yen, to ensure the stability and credibility of the country's financial system.

Japan will be better able to cope with any future financial failures after the establishment of new entities and the expansion of existing systems to cope with problem loans, he said. Matsushita urged the regional banks to take care of problem loans as soon as possible to regain credibility among depositors and to step up risk management.

On industrial output, Matsushita said that this was on a gradual upward trend as seen in the rebound in demand, despite stock adjustments in industries such as semiconductors. Corporate capital spending and private consumption were also recovering, he added.
